author: !I RECOMMEND THIS GAME!
title: Dear Subway Surfers-
content:
Subway Surfers is one of those games that you can pick up for five minutes and somehow end up playing for an hour. It’s incredibly fun, easy to understand, and has that perfect “one more run” feeling that keeps you coming back.

One of the biggest things that makes Subway Surfers so good is how simple the gameplay is. You don’t need a complicated tutorial or a bunch of confusing controls. You swipe left, right, up, and down, dodge obstacles, collect coins, and try to get the highest score possible. Even though the controls are simple, getting really good at the game takes practice and quick reactions.

Another amazing part of Subway Surfers is the amount of content. There are tons of characters, outfits, hoverboards, locations, and collectibles to discover. The game also constantly gives you things to work toward, so it doesn’t feel like you’ve completed everything after playing for a few days.

The different locations are also a huge reason the game stays interesting. Traveling to different cities and seeing new environments makes each update feel different. The scenery, music, characters, and overall style give the game a lot of personality.

And let’s talk about the nostalgia. Subway Surfers has been around for years, and so many people remember playing it when they were younger. It’s one of those games that can bring back memories just by hearing the music or seeing the familiar characters running down the tracks.

The game is also great for quick sessions. If you only have a few minutes, you can play a couple of runs. If you have more time, you can keep going and try to beat your high score. It works whether you want something casual or you want to seriously challenge yourself.

The best part, though, is that Subway Surfers is just FUN. There doesn’t have to be some complicated reason behind it. Running through the subway, dodging trains, grabbing coins, using power-ups, and trying to survive as long as possible is satisfying every single time.

Overall, Subway Surfers deserves a huge amount of credit for becoming such a recognizable and long-lasting mobile game. Its simple controls, colorful style, huge amount of content, constant goals, memorable characters, and addictive gameplay make it incredibly easy to come back to.

10/10 game. 🚇🔥

If you’re looking for a game that’s easy to learn, fun to play, and almost impossible to get completely bored of, Subway Surfers is absolutely worth playing.

author: Yehya Kader
title: Love the game, but something happened...
content: I have had subway surfers for a long, long time and I have learned all the tricks, unlocked tons of characters and hover boards, maxed out just about everything and I wasn’t thinking about deleting until today. I had been saving up hover boards, keys, headstarts, and score boosters for one round where I would go all out and get a giant high score. I began my round perfectly and everything was going smoothly. But a round like this, obviously, would take days to finish. Being not done with my round, I left my app open like I always do when I want to continue a run and just turned off my phone. Keep in mind that the app was open in my quick select and I did not power off my phone. I tapped the button on the side of my phone to simply put it to sleep, leaving my app open as I ALWAYS do when I want to continue my run and it ALWAYS works. The next day when I woke up, I turned on my phone to continue my run, and I was speechless to see that the hours and hover boards, keys, head starts, and a score of 20 million SO FAR had all been deleted. The game restarted even though I left my app open. If it had not restarted, I would have began right where I left off, on 20 million. And even when I checked my high score (my previous one was 11 million) to see if it had changed, it was still on 11 million! The least the game could have done to make up for all the wasted things I had used was to at least give me the score I died on. Many other times, I have wanted to continue a run like this, but the game restarts. I would like Kiloo Games to please make an option where the players can return to their run instead of restarting from the start again, and I think many players would agree with me. If this solution does not go into affect, I would honestly have no other choice but to delete the game which is something I do not want to do because I love Subway Surfers. I know that Kiloo Games will probably not read this, but if there is a chance you do, please consider this.
